title: Observed event payment is not a monotonic measure of annual medical-bill problems
source_unit: 2024 MEPS event records linked to HC-256 annual person context

denominator.unit: positive-weight office events with valid annual bill-problem context and payment

observations.method: HC-254G event PERWT24F with VARSTR/VARPSU Taylor linearization; event payment conditioned on HC-256 PROBPY42 annual person context.
observations.uncertainty: No causal estimate; annual context is not an event-level bill key and event users are a selected population.
observations.subgroup: Office events split by whether the linked person reported a 2024 medical bill problem.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower event self/family payment among bill-problem reporters may reflect coverage, event mix, prior bills, or other selection rather than protection.

denominator.unit: positive-weight ER events with valid annual bill-problem context and payment

observations.method: HC-254E event PERWT24F with VARSTR/VARPSU Taylor linearization; event payment conditioned on HC-256 PROBPY42 annual person context.
observations.uncertainty: No causal estimate; annual context is not an event-level bill key, and positive-payment/weighted event universes are selected.
observations.subgroup: Emergency-room events split by whether the linked person reported a 2024 medical bill problem.
observations.counterinterpretation: The small difference does not establish that the ER event caused the bill problem or that payment captures burden.

denominator.unit: positive-weight inpatient events with valid annual bill-problem context and payment

observations.method: HC-254D event PERWT24F with VARSTR/VARPSU Taylor linearization; event payment conditioned on HC-256 PROBPY42 annual person context.
observations.uncertainty: No causal estimate; annual context is not an event-level bill key, and the bill-problem cell has only 238 valid event records.
observations.subgroup: Inpatient events split by whether the linked person reported a 2024 medical bill problem.
observations.counterinterpretation: The higher mean is compatible with burden but cannot separate event severity, coverage, prior balances, or other causes.

denominator.unit: positive-weight prescription events with valid annual bill-problem context and payment

observations.method: HC-254A event PERWT24F with VARSTR/VARPSU Taylor linearization; event payment conditioned on HC-256 PROBPY42 annual person context.
observations.uncertainty: No causal estimate; purchase events exclude non-purchasers and annual context is not an event-level bill key.
observations.subgroup: Prescription purchases split by whether the linked person reported a 2024 medical bill problem.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower observed payment among bill-problem reporters may reflect medication mix, coverage, subsidies, or selection into observed purchases.

boundary: This joins observed event payments to annual person context, not a specific bill or causal event sequence. It does not observe forgone care, debt, payment timing, borrowing, savings draw, recovery, trust, or action.
